title: Excel COUNT Says 2 but You Have 4 Values? Here's Why #Shorts
description: A visual, original fictional learning example from FlowMinute Lab. In this fictional Excel column, there are four filled cells, but COUNT returns only two. Why the mismatch? Learn the safe verification step using the official product guidance below. Original diagrams and synthetic English narration; not a real account or software screen capture. Official source: https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/excel/ways-to-count-values-in-a-worksheet #FlowMinuteLab #TechTips

scenes.title: COUNT MISSED THE TEXT
scenes.narration: In this fictional Excel column, there are four filled cells, but COUNT returns only two. Why the mismatch?

scenes.title: WHAT COUNT COUNTS
scenes.narration: Microsoft explains COUNT counts numeric entries in a range. Text labels are not counted as numbers.

scenes.title: WHAT COUNTA COUNTS
scenes.narration: COUNTA counts cells that contain data, including text. It answers a different question from COUNT.

scenes.title: ONE SPECIAL CATCH
scenes.narration: Microsoft notes that COUNTA can count formulas returning empty text. Visually blank isn't always truly empty.

scenes.title: PICK THE RIGHT TEST
scenes.narration: Use COUNT for numeric entries and COUNTA for nonempty entries. Check sample rows before trusting any total.
